title: Jurisdiction in representative litigation
summary: Class litigation raises separate questions about subject-matter jurisdiction, Article III injury, personal jurisdiction, and venue. The relevance of absent members differs among these inquiries.
notes: Certification cannot supply missing jurisdiction, and one decision about absentees’ status cannot be generalized to every requirement.

sections.Meaning: Class litigation raises separate questions about subject-matter jurisdiction, Article III injury, personal jurisdiction, and venue. The relevance of absent members differs among these inquiries.
sections.How to work through the question: Identify the jurisdictional basis and the particular requirement. Compare ordinary diversity with CAFA, TransUnion’s concrete-injury requirement for individual damages, Shutts’s protection of absent plaintiffs, and Mussat’s treatment of defendant contacts.
